claims: Mobileye's first-half 2026 revenue growth and SuperVision volume growth coexist with lower operating cash flow, higher capital expenditure and a $591 million net cash acquisition outlay, so commercial momentum should not be treated as equivalent to improving cash conversion.

Average System Price declined 1% in the first half because of a higher mix of lower-ASP Chinese OEM sales, providing a primary-source downside mechanism through mix/pricing even as advanced-product volumes grow.

The TSMC manufacturing agreement adds supply-chain redundancy, but STMicroelectronics remains an established EyeQ manufacturing partner; resilience has improved incrementally rather than supplier dependence being eliminated.

Current revenue remains substantially derived from commercially deployed ADAS while newer advanced ADAS/AV products approach production, so the core cash-generating base and newer Physical-AI optionality should remain analytically separated.
causalEdges: lower-ASP China OEM mix -> lower average system price -> potential pressure on unit economics
advanced-product growth + acquisition/capex expansion -> higher capital demands -> cash-conversion sensitivity
second foundry pathway -> manufacturing redundancy -> lower single-supplier fragility, conditional on production allocation and ramp
ADAS installed base -> current revenue anchor -> resilience while newer autonomy businesses remain execution-dependent

risks.risk: Operating cash flow fell to $210 million from $322 million in the first half while property-and-equipment purchases rose and the Mentee acquisition used $591 million net cash; expansion therefore raises capital-allocation and cash-conversion sensitivity.
A higher mix of lower-ASP China OEM sales reduced Average System Price, creating a measurable mix/pricing pressure that stronger volumes must offset.
Manufacturing diversification is incomplete: the TSMC agreement improves redundancy but does not establish supplier independence or disclose future production allocation.

contradictions: Revenue and advanced-product volumes improved while operating cash flow declined and capital demands increased; growth evidence therefore does not by itself prove improving cash economics.
Supply-chain redundancy is improving, but the evidence does not support treating foundry concentration as fully resolved.
unknowns: How much of the first-half operating-cash-flow decline reflects timing versus a durable change in cash conversion.
Future EyeQ production allocation and ramp timing between STMicroelectronics and TSMC.
Whether richer advanced-product mix can sustainably offset lower ASP in parts of the OEM mix and earn attractive returns on incremental capital.
falsifiers: Sustained operating-cash-flow growth that outpaces incremental capital demands while advanced products scale would weaken the cash-conversion concern.
Evidence of stable or improving realized ASP/gross-profit economics despite China mix would weaken the pricing-mix concern.
Demonstrated high-volume dual-source production with disclosed allocation resilience would weaken the remaining supplier-concentration concern.
